After EUR/GBP Trade 1 was closed, the account history looks like this.

Lessons: 1. Still missing the correct entry points - reason for entry is not good enough. Possible remedy: Look further left and left again to determine if the zone we want to trade is a zone that was set up to be broken.

2. Price turns at SL level - my SL level in the previous trade is the optimum entry price level. Possible remedy: learn why price turned at SL level and Also, I have a question to all of you regarding platform data and how you would determine which is the more accurate information.

I have provided charts from two MT4 brokers - Pepperstone and FXPro, and one chart from JForex - Dukascopy.

This is where I get confused on which data to trust. The difference in the high value is very different for the spike in 7 Oct 2016 Pepperstone FXPro Dukascopy Dukascopy high was at 0.93260. FXPro high was at 0.92627. Pepperstone high was at 0.92635.

For me, I would use the MT4 data since I have another source to compare with. But the huge difference in value with JForex makes me wonder which data to trust. Really need help on this. How do you all cope with these types of issues?

Hey Frosty. I have noticed similar differences in the past between brokers. One of my feed was about 2 pips off from the other constantly. But that meant that the reaction was also off. So it was fine, as long as you pick your levels from the charts your are going to trade on. So that is my experience. Stick to one feed.:)

Thank you for your reply, Zee. I will stick to one feed next time around. So from your experience this issue shouldn't have a major impact on our PA signals then? (assuming there is no pattern in the # of pips difference between different feeds)

The reason I use pepperstone feed to do the analysis is because they somehow have a lot more history than FXPro feed.

Dunno if that is specific to my MT4 only or applies to everyone's. I've set the ‘Max bars in history’ and ‘Max bars in chart’ as "2147483647"

Yes, from my experience it is not an issue. The only problem can be, if you do your charting from one feed and your trading from another. Then the level you base your SL on for example might be a few pips higher or lower on your "real" feed than on your charting one. I think it's simpler to use just one. But more experienced traders might have better advice about this. So let's wait for more replies.

All the technical knowledge in the World is useless if we can't learn to get out of our own way

Thanks for dropping by, IF I trust that by banishing our own inner demons, we can get a happier life as well.

RTM has been a true blessing for me as I am also learning life lessons here, not just technical trading methods.

Mine basically stems from lack of confidence, and the root of that comes from a harsh criticizing and judging environment when I grow up.

I am always second-guessing, not confident of my own answers and actions, and this shows not just in my trading, but also in other aspects of my life.

The fear of critics and judgements literally immobilized me from doing anything.

My thought process was: "If I don't do anything, I won't find myself in situations where I could be judged and criticized". This definitely slows me down in all aspects of life.

Regarding trading, I used to think that I will become confident when I can pinpoint perfect entries and exits without any losing trade. I know now that this is not true. Losses do occur and our attitude as a trader is to accept them and embrace them as part of our profession. Confidence first, then method will take a solid form over time, not instantly.

Thanks to RTM, I am now forcing myself to just do things that are aligned with my goals. It was not comfortable at first, but as time passes, I see no reason why I should have those kinds of fears. I am starting to lose weight (so I don't die from a sudden heart attack due to obesity) and eliminated my road rage problem for a start Still have many more goals to achieve.

I'm learning to trust the process, and that is what matters currently. As many people used to say, Rome wasn't built in a day (Don't know why everytime I post psychological issues, it turns out quite lengthy Maybe its because I feel at home here with friends. Please pardon the sidetrack everybody)
If you have a couple of minutes, read this. It might help you!:) waitbutwhy.com/2014/06/taming-mammoth-le...inions-run-life.html Cheers, Z.
